n: At night the bride searches for the one she loves but cannot find him. This may be a dream or a poetic picture of longing.

f.g: Repeated four times in verses 1–4 — her whole being longs for him.

n: She resolves to get up and search the city streets and squares for him, but still doesn’t find him.
The city watchmen find her, and she asks if they have seen her beloved.

f.g: Night guards who patrolled the city.

n: Soon after, she finds him and holds on tight, bringing him to her mother’s house — a sign of honorable, family-approved love.
The refrain returns: don’t awaken love until it is ready.

f.r: Song of Solomon 2:7; Song of Solomon 8:4

n: A new scene: a wedding procession appears from the wilderness, rising like columns of smoke from burning incense and fragrant spices.

f.g: Columns of incense smoke — or the dust raised by a great procession.

n: Here comes Solomon’s royal carriage, guarded by sixty of Israel’s mightiest soldiers.

f.g: A litter or sedan chair carried by bearers.

n: Each guard is skilled in battle, sword at his side, ready to defend against any danger in the night.
Solomon built this carriage from the fine timber of Lebanon.

f.g: A palanquin — an elegant covered carriage.

n: Its posts were silver, its base gold, its seat purple, and its interior lovingly decorated by the women of Jerusalem.

f.g: An expensive dye used for royalty.

n: The women of Zion are invited to come and see King Solomon wearing the crown his mother placed on him on his wedding day, the happiest day of his life.
